purpose: Independent smoke-test evaluation of Phase 4 Lesson Reconciliation quality. No prior scores are included.

lesson.title: Modelos de Extração de Características e APIs
lesson.description: O objetivo deste encontro é comparar os sistemas implementados utilizando modelos com Embedding Words e os modelos baseados em extração de características. Ao término do encontro, espera-se que as pessoas desenvolvedoras possam estar familiarizadas com as características comuns destes sistemas e suas peculiaridades de implementação. Também será realizada uma familiarização com o desenvolvimento de API Python.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Boolean AND operator
before_phase4_candidates.description: The AND operator narrows database search results by requiring all specified terms to be present in the resulting records. It is used to combine multiple concepts, making the search more specific.
coverage_criteria: Define the effect of AND on search result count.
Provide an example query using AND.
Explain when to use AND to focus a search.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article dedicates a section titled 'Using AND' that explains the purpose, gives examples, and includes a Venn diagram. It states 'Use AND in a search to narrow your results' and provides the example 'cloning AND humans AND ethics'.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: AND is a single, well-defined operator with clear usage, making it suitable for a focused assessment item.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Boolean OR operator
before_phase4_candidates.description: The OR operator broadens database search results by including records that contain any of the specified terms. It is used to connect synonyms or related concepts.
coverage_criteria: Define the effect of OR on search result count.
Provide an example query using OR.
Explain when to use OR to broaden a search.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article includes a 'Using OR' section that describes OR as connecting similar concepts and broadening results, with the example 'cloning OR genetics OR reproduction' and a Venn diagram.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: OR is a distinct Boolean operator with a clearly opposite function to AND, allowing it to be taught and assessed as a standalone concept.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Boolean NOT operator
before_phase4_candidates.description: The NOT operator narrows search results by excluding records that contain a specified term. It is used to remove unwanted concepts from a search.
coverage_criteria: Define the effect of NOT on search results.
Provide an example query using NOT.
Explain a scenario where NOT would be useful.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source has a dedicated 'Using NOT' section that explains it excludes words and narrows the search, with the example 'cloning NOT sheep'.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: NOT is a fundamental Boolean operator that completes the trio, and its exclusionary behavior is distinct from AND and OR, justifying separate treatment.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Phrase searching with quotes
before_phase4_candidates.description: Phrase searching involves enclosing multiple words in quotes to ensure they appear together as a contiguous phrase in search results. This technique increases specificity when used with Boolean operators like AND.
coverage_criteria: Explain how phrase searching affects search results.
Construct a query that combines phrase searching with Boolean AND.
Identify when phrase searching is appropriate to avoid irrelevant results.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Within the 'Using AND' section, the source states: 'You can search using phrases to make your results more specific. For example: "college students" AND "test anxiety".' This explicitly presents phrase searching as a complementary technique to Boolean operators.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Phrase searching is a discrete search refinement technique that can be checked with a few practical questions about syntax and effect.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Implied AND in databases
before_phase4_candidates.description: In many databases and search engines like Google, the AND operator is automatically inserted between search terms. Users should be aware that this may cause terms to be searched individually rather than as a phrase.
coverage_criteria: Identify the behavior of implied AND in a search engine.
Describe a potential pitfall of implied AND.
Suggest a solution to improve search precision when implied AND causes issues.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source warns: 'In many, but not all, databases, the AND is implied. For example, Google automatically puts an AND in between your search terms.' This highlights a key nuance of Boolean search behavior that can lead to unexpected results.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Implied AND is a specific behavioral aspect of search systems that can be assessed through explanation and example-based questions.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Boolean search order and parentheses grouping
before_phase4_candidates.description: Databases typically evaluate AND before OR. To change the order or group ORed terms together, parentheses must be used, e.g., ethics AND (cloning OR reproductive techniques).
coverage_criteria: Explain why search order matters in Boolean queries.
Rewrite a query using parentheses to control evaluation order.
Predict the result of a mixed Boolean query without parentheses.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The 'Search order' section explicitly states: 'Databases usually recognize AND as the primary operator, and will connect concepts with AND together first. If you use a combination of AND and OR operators in a search, enclose the words to be "ORed" together in parentheses.' Examples are provided.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Search order and parentheses usage form a self-contained lesson in Boolean logic that is testable with practical query construction exercises.

before_phase4_candidates.label: Boolean operators as mathematical sets
before_phase4_candidates.description: Boolean operators are based on mathematical set theory and Venn diagrams, providing a visual way to understand how search terms intersect (AND), combine (OR), or exclude (NOT).
coverage_criteria: Map the AND operation to a Venn diagram intersection.
Explain how OR corresponds to union in set theory.
Relate the concept of sets to database search results.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The opening section states: 'Boolean operators form the basis of mathematical sets and database logic.' Venn diagrams are used throughout to illustrate AND and OR operations, grounding the abstract operators in visual set representations.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Understanding the set-theoretic foundation of Boolean operators is a conceptual prerequisite that can be assessed by asking students to interpret and draw Venn diagrams for given queries.

coverage_criteria: Can write code that loads text data and applies a feature extraction method (e.g., using scikit-learn's CountVectorizer).
Can describe common Python libraries used for NLP feature extraction (e.g., NLTK, spaCy, scikit-learn).
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept directly derived from workbook metadata, covering the practical coding aspect of NLP feature extraction within the lesson.

reconciled_candidates.label: Comparing word embeddings and feature extraction for NLP
reconciled_candidates.description: Contrasting NLP systems built with pre-trained word embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec) against those based on traditional feature extraction methods, covering trade-offs in dimensionality and semantic capture.
coverage_criteria: Can identify differences in input representation between embedding-based and feature extraction-based NLP models.
Can discuss trade-offs (e.g., dimensionality, semantic capture) between the two approaches.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept from workbook metadata, aligning with the lesson's objective to compare modeling paradigms.

reconciled_candidates.label: Deploying NLP models via a Python API
reconciled_candidates.description: Developing a Python-based REST API to serve or integrate NLP models, using frameworks like Flask or FastAPI, and addressing deployment considerations such as latency and data serialization.
coverage_criteria: Can outline steps to wrap an NLP model into a simple REST API using Python (e.g., Flask, FastAPI).
Can identify challenges in serving NLP models via APIs (e.g., latency, data serialization).
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Standalone concept from workbook metadata, fulfilling the lesson's goal of API development familiarity within the NLP domain.

reconciled_candidates.label: Flask application basics: setup, run, and debug mode
reconciled_candidates.description: Creating a minimal Flask app, running the development server, and enabling debug mode for auto-reload and interactive debugging, while understanding its inappropriateness for production.
coverage_criteria: Can write a minimal Flask app with one route returning HTML.
Can start the Flask development server with flask run and specify the app module.
Can enable debug mode and explain why it is unsafe for production.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: These candidates together cover the essential steps to initialize, run, and configure a Flask project in development mode, forming a single foundational concept.

reconciled_candidates.label: Routing, URL building, and HTTP method handling in Flask
reconciled_candidates.description: Defining routes with decorators, capturing dynamic URL variables with converters, managing canonical URLs and trailing slash behavior, building URLs with url_for(), and handling different HTTP methods.
coverage_criteria: Can define a route with a dynamic path segment and a converter (e.g., int:post_id).
Can explain the trailing slash redirect behavior.
Can use url_for() to generate a URL for a view function.
Can create a route that responds to both GET and POST requests.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: These candidates all pertain to defining and managing HTTP request handling in Flask. They are tightly interdependent and form a cohesive unit on routing patterns.

reconciled_candidates.label: HTML escaping for security in Flask
reconciled_candidates.description: Preventing XSS attacks by escaping user-supplied data in HTML using markupsafe.escape(); understanding that Jinja templates auto-escape by default.
coverage_criteria: Can explain why HTML escaping is necessary.
Can use markupsafe.escape() on user input in a Flask route.
Can state that Jinja auto-escapes variables in templates.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a critical security practice that is isolated enough to form its own small concept, ensuring focused attention.

reconciled_candidates.label: Serving static files and rendering Jinja templates
reconciled_candidates.description: Serving static assets from the 'static' directory via /static/<path>, and rendering dynamic HTML pages with Jinja templates stored in a 'templates' folder, using render_template() with variable passing.
coverage_criteria: Can use url_for('static', filename='style.css') to link a CSS file.
Can create a Jinja template that displays a variable and uses an {% if %} block.
Can explain the default directory structure for static and template files.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Static file serving and template rendering are closely related view-layer concerns that are often taught together; merging creates a more cohesive concept.

reconciled_candidates.label: Flask context locals and test_request_context()
reconciled_candidates.description: Understanding that Flask uses thread-local proxies for request, session, etc., and using app.test_request_context() to simulate an HTTP request for testing.
coverage_criteria: Can explain that `request` is a proxy to a thread-local object.
Can write a test that uses test_request_context() to access request.path.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate introduces a specific concept that addresses common confusion for beginners; it stands alone as a testable idea.

notes_for_judge: Do not assume a candidate is good because it is source-backed.
Review means not accepted and not pruned; in some cases it may be a deterministic fallback after omission.
Judge against the lesson metadata and the project concept definition, not against labels only.
